fair_value_policy: Fair Value V2.1 is the sole valuation baseline. This event must not directly overwrite official numeric macro series or Fair Value.

observed_evidence.shipping_traffic: Reuters reported preliminary ship-tracking data showing only four commodity vessels exited and ten entered the Gulf through the Strait of Hormuz over the weekend, below a 10-day average of about 14 commodity-vessel movements per day. Before the Iran war began on February 28, the strait typically handled about 125 large commercial vessel transits per day and roughly 20% of global crude-oil and LNG supply.
observed_evidence.maritime_security: UKMTO reported a vessel was struck by an unknown projectile while transiting Hormuz on September 13; crew status, damage and environmental impact were initially unknown.
observed_evidence.access_restrictions: Reuters reported Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority issued an updated list of 77 vessels accused of violating Iranian passage protocols, warning of fines, detention or confiscation and urging insurers, P&I clubs and classification societies to stop serving listed vessels.
observed_evidence.alternative_routes: Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline remained temporarily shut following a drone attack, while Bab el-Mandeb commodity-vessel traffic over the weekend was broadly near its recent 10-day average.

semantic_interpretation: The new information confirms that the Hormuz shock remains a physical-flow and maritime-access problem rather than only a price or diplomatic-risk signal. Persistently depressed traffic, direct vessel-security incidents, and an expanded vessel-sanctions regime raise the probability of prolonged tanker availability, insurance, freight and delivered-energy cost pressure even if headline crude production is unchanged.
